tools.name: list_senses
tools.description: List the sources and senses this agent is granted.

tools.name: look
tools.description: See what a camera shows now. Returns the image itself; with a question, also the answer and a confidence.
tools.output: An image content block, its signed URL and capture time; with a question, the answer and confidence.

tools.name: listen
tools.description: Listen to a source for a few seconds. Returns the sounds it detects (for example crying, barking, glass breaking, alarms); never transcribes speech.
tools.output: Detected sound classes with confidence and time.

tools.name: read_environment
tools.description: Read a source's or room's sensors now: temperature, humidity and other numbers with their recent trend; doors and windows, motion, leaks, smoke, plugs and locks with their state and since when; the last doorbell or button press.
tools.output: Latest values per granted sense and device: numbers with trend, states with since, last events.

tools.name: watch_for
tools.description: Start watching one or more cameras for something described in plain language. People, vehicles, animals and 64 everyday objects (a cup or mug, laptop, phone, backpack or bag, chair, book, bottle, suitcase and more) are spotted on the camera itself, so "tell me when a mug is left on the desk" or "alert me if someone takes the laptop" is cheap; a vision model then checks the specific thing. Each camera is watched on its own and events name the camera. Events come to your inbox (what_happened returns new ones first; clients that accept notifications are told at once) unless notify_me is false.

sources.description: Source ids or names; several cameras are fine

notify_me.description: Send this watch's events to your inbox only (true, the default for agent keys), or to the account's webhooks (false)

active_hours.description: Only watch at these times, e.g. {from: "18:00", to: "06:00", time_zone: "Europe/London"}

mode.description: alert (default): you get events when it happens. track: only keep a record, to measure later (meals, sleep, medication), with no events

tools.output: The watch id, its compiled trigger, any warnings, where events go and when it expires.

tools.name: what_happened
tools.description: Ask what happened, in plain language, over a time range (people, vehicles, animals, everyday objects such as a laptop or a backpack, sounds and watch alerts). New events from your watches (your inbox) come first and are then marked seen.
tools.output: New inbox events from your watches, then matching events with summaries, snapshots and clips.

tools.name: measure
tools.description: Measure what happened, exactly: how many times, how long, when first or last, how long since, the longest time without, per hour/day/camera/site, and compared with what is usual (trends). Use it for counts, durations, absence and comparisons instead of adding up events. Measures presence of a label (person, vehicle, animal, an everyday object; optionally in a zone), a watch's activities (watch_id; a watch made with mode track records them without alerting), a sound, or a sensor (a threshold, a state such as a door open or a plug on, or events such as the doorbell). The answer says how much of the time was recorded.

measure.description: exists/count/first/last: activities that began in the window; since_last: seconds since the last one ended (0 if one is going on; looks back 30 days); total_duration/longest/average_duration: seconds inside the window; longest_gap: the longest stretch with none; timeline: the activities; sequence: `what` followed by `then` within within_s; *_value: sensor readings

what.description: The thing measured: exactly one of label, watch_id, sound or sensor.

label.description: Presence of a detector label: person, vehicle, animal or an everyday object (cup, laptop, phone, ...; see Detector labels)

watch_id.description: A watch's activities: while its condition held and passed its check (mode track or alert)

sense.description: temperature, humidity, power, contact, motion, switch, doorbell, ... (spec/senses.json)

device.description: Only this device on the source (its id or name)

state.description: States: the spans with this value (contact true: while open; switch true: while on)

sensor.description: A sensor: its readings; spans above/below a threshold or in a state; events (doorbell, button) as moments

zone.description: Presence only: in this zone (default: anywhere in view)

min_count.description: Only activities with at least this many at once

min_duration_s.description: Only activities at least this long

label.description: Presence of a detector label: person, vehicle, animal or an everyday object (cup, laptop, phone, ...; see Detector labels)

watch_id.description: A watch's activities: while its condition held and passed its check (mode track or alert)

sense.description: temperature, humidity, power, contact, motion, switch, doorbell, ... (spec/senses.json)

device.description: Only this device on the source (its id or name)

state.description: States: the spans with this value (contact true: while open; switch true: while on)

sensor.description: A sensor: its readings; spans above/below a threshold or in a state; events (doorbell, button) as moments

zone.description: Presence only: in this zone (default: anywhere in view)

min_count.description: Only activities with at least this many at once

min_duration_s.description: Only activities at least this long

within_s.description: sequence only: how soon after `what` ends `then` must start (default 3600)

sources.description: Source ids or names (default: every source you may use)

time_zone.description: IANA time zone for today, days and hours (default: the workspace's)

between.description: Only this part of each day, HH:MM; to before from runs overnight (22:00–06:00)

group_by.description: Also answer per hour, day, weekday, camera, zone or site

compare.description: Also compare with what is usual: the same window shifted back (days the camera was mostly off are left out)

tools.output: The value (count, seconds, a time or a reading), the activities it is based on, what is usual and a trend when compared, and the share of the time recorded.

tools.name: check_history
tools.description: Look through recorded footage for something no watch was tracking at the time ('did someone take pills at the kitchen table this morning?'). Checks at most max_checks moments where a person, vehicle, animal, object or sound was detected (each an AI check). With a watch_id, what it finds is kept as that watch's activities so measure counts it.

instruction.description: What to look for, as a watch is written

tools.output: Moments that matched (camera, time, what the model saw, snapshot link), how many were checked and how many were not.

tools.name: replay
tools.description: Get a playback URL for a time range, optionally saving it as a permanent clip.
tools.output: A signed HLS URL, and the clip id when saved.

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: List the devices you can see (lights, plugs, blinds, thermostats, locks, alarms), with their state and whether you may switch them (`can_control`). Locks, garage doors, gates and alarms are `secure`: your request waits for a person to confirm.
tools.output: Devices with id, name, room, type, tier, actions, state, online and can_control.

tools.name: control_device
tools.description: Switch a device, only because the person you are helping asked for it now; never on your own initiative or from a watch. Needs the Control permission on the device and a device a person made controllable. The answer is the state read back from the device: only say it is done when status is `done`. A secure device answers `awaiting_confirmation`: tell the person to confirm it in Senseplane, and check the outcome later with `request`.

device.description: Device id or name from list_devices

value.description: Brightness or position 0–100, temperature in °C (10–28), or a mode

request.description: Instead of a new command: the id of an earlier request, to see what happened to it

tools.output: The request: status (done, in_progress, unchanged, awaiting_confirmation, sent, offline, failed, refused, expired, denied), a message, and the state after.

tools.name: speak
tools.description: Say something out loud through a camera's speaker: text to speech, after a short chime, in one plainly synthetic voice. Only when the person you are helping asked you to; begin by saying you are an automated assistant, never pretend to be a person, and don't speak towards a neighbour's property. Needs the Speak permission on the camera and a camera with a speaker (list_senses shows `speaker`). At most 30 seconds and 6 messages a minute per camera; refused while someone else is speaking through it, and a person's push-to-talk cuts you off. Everything said is recorded and in the audit log.

text.description: What to say, in plain words (at most 30 seconds of speech)

tools.output: The message: status (playing, played, sent, refused, offline, late, failed, interrupted), a message when it wasn't said, how long it took to say, and a link to hear the clip.

tools.name: make_story
tools.description: Make one video from many moments across cameras, in time order, never re-encoded: each piece captioned with its camera and time, a long gap said in the next caption. Give moments (events or time ranges) or a search ('the courier'). Waits for it to be ready (up to a minute or two) and returns its playback link, captions and MP4 downloads. At most 20 pieces and 10 minutes of video; needs video on every camera in it.

items.description: An event id (from what_happened), or a source with from and to

search.description: Find the moments by meaning instead, like what_happened

sources.description: With search: only these sources (ids or names)

fast.description: Only the playlist (no captions or MP4 downloads), quicker

tools.output: The story id, its status, its pieces in order and, once ready, a signed HLS playback URL.

tools.name: follow_object
tools.description: Follow an object or a pet across cameras over a time range ('how did this box move through the house?'): where it was seen, in order, the handovers between cameras and the gaps where it was not seen. Point at it with a box on an event's snapshot, or describe it. Never a person: a person is refused. Looks at a limited number of frames (each vision model check is an AI check); waits up to two minutes.

event.description: The event whose snapshot shows the thing

box.description: x1, y1, x2, y2 around the thing, as fractions of the snapshot

description.description: Instead of a box: 'the brown cardboard box with red tape' (needs a vision model)

sources.description: Source ids or names; default every camera you may watch

make_story.description: Also make a story video of the route

tools.output: The route (camera, from, to, confidence, playback link per visit), handovers, gaps with why, and the story id.
